regions.name: Central Sahel
regions.summary: Military juntas in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger expelled French and UN forces, turned to Russian security partners, and asserted state control over gold and uranium.

regions.name: Lake Chad basin
regions.summary: Lake Chad shrank about 90% between 1963 and 2001; Chad ended its defence pact with France in Nov 2024.

regions.name: Sudan
regions.summary: SAF-RSF war since April 2023, with drones from Turkey and Iran on the SAF side and UAE-linked supply and gold networks on the RSF side.

regions.name: Great Lakes and eastern DRC
regions.summary: M23 holds mining areas in North Kivu; UN experts documented Rwandan troops alongside it. The US brokered a 2025 peace and minerals framework.

regions.name: Central African Rep.
regions.summary: Wagner-linked firms hold gold rights, including Ndassima.

regions.name: Horn and Red Sea
regions.summary: Ethiopia opened GERD in Sept 2025 over Egyptian objections; AFRICOM ran 124 strikes in Somalia in 2025.

regions.name: Coastal West Africa spillover
regions.summary: Ghana artisanal gold reached 39% of output in 2024; Lekki port (CHEC 52.5%) and Cote d'Ivoire's Baleine field anchor the coast. Sahel jihadist spillover entries still pending.

regions.name: Southern Africa
regions.summary: Mozambique LNG in insurgency-hit Cabo Delgado restarted Oct 2025.

regions.name: North Africa
regions.summary: Libya's oil is split between rival authorities; the east-based government shut fields in Aug 2024.

links.actions: UN Group of Experts reported 3,000-4,000 Rwanda Defence Force troops operating in North Kivu alongside M23.
links.returns: Coltan from M23-held Rubaya traced into Rwandan supply chains.
links.position: Rwanda denies supporting M23 and cites the FDLR threat on its border.

links.actions: UN Panel found allegations of UAE arms deliveries to the RSF via eastern Chad credible; OFAC designated seven UAE-based companies that supplied the RSF with money and equipment.
links.returns: Sudanese gold bought by UAE-based AZ Gold and moved to Dubai; account accessible to RSF procurement chief.
links.position: The UAE denies arming any party and says its flights carry humanitarian aid; the OFAC targets are private firms, not the UAE state.

links.actions: SWISSAID found 405 t of African gold imported into the UAE in 2022 was not declared as exports by African countries; 80-85% of African ASM gold went to the UAE.
links.returns: Gold refining and trade volume for Dubai; undeclared value of about US$30.7bn for 2022 smuggling.
links.position: The UAE has said it is tightening due-diligence rules for gold refiners.

links.actions: Reuters (2021) reported the proposed Wagner deal at about $10.8m a month for ~1,000 fighters (terms not independently confirmed). Wagner left Mali in June 2025; the Kremlin-controlled Africa Corps stayed, about 70-80% ex-Wagner.
links.returns: Stake for Russia's Yadran Group in the Bamako gold refinery (see ru-mali-gold).
links.position: Bamako and Moscow describe it as state-to-state security cooperation.

links.actions: Construction of a 200 t/yr gold refinery began June 2025; Mali holds 62%, Yadran and a Swiss investor the rest.
links.returns: Minority stake in refining of Malian gold.
links.position: Mali presents it as ending raw-gold exports and asserting economic sovereignty.

links.actions: OFAC: Wagner-linked Midas holds rights to the Ndassima gold mine and with Wagner denied CAR inspectors access; Diamville converted CAR gold into dollars.
links.returns: Ndassima gold rights (deposit assessed >US$1bn) and CAR gold and diamond trade.
links.position: CAR's government describes Russian personnel as instructors invited under a bilateral agreement.

links.actions: Contract and end-user records show Baykar sent at least US$120m of weapons, including TB2 drones and hundreds of warheads, to the SAF in 2024.
links.returns: Not public in sources used (sale revenue only).
links.position: Baykar did not deny the sale in the cited report; Ankara backs the SAF-led government as Sudan's legitimate authority.

links.actions: Satellite imagery showed a Mohajer-6 at the SAF's Wadi Sayyidna base (Jan 2024); six Qeshm Fars Air cargo flights went from Iran to Port Sudan in Dec 2023-Jan 2024.
links.returns: Not established. WSJ reported (Mar 2024) Iran sought a Red Sea base in return; Sudan and Iran both denied it. Diplomatic ties restored in 2023.
links.position: A senior SAF source denied the drones came directly from Iran.

links.actions: Satellite images showed a Turkish-made Akinci combat drone at Egypt's East Oweinat airstrip near the Sudan border in Dec 2025.
links.returns: No material return documented; Reuters describes Egypt's interest as a SAF-run state aligned with Cairo on Nile water (GERD) and border security.
links.position: Cairo backs Sudan's state institutions and the army as the legitimate authority.

links.actions: Amended Sicomines deal (2024): Chinese partners to fund up to US$7bn of infrastructure, tied to copper prices.
links.position: Kinshasa says the renegotiation raised its share of benefits.

links.actions: 1,306 loan commitments worth US$182.28bn, 2000-2023 (commitments, not disbursements).
links.returns: Varies by loan; resource-backed in some cases (not itemised here).
links.position: Beijing frames lending as development finance with no political conditions.

links.actions: Brokered the 27 June 2025 DRC-Rwanda peace agreement and a Regional Economic Integration Framework on critical-mineral supply chains (signed 4 Dec 2025).
links.returns: Framework for US-linked investment in DRC and Rwanda mineral supply chains.
links.position: Washington presents it as peace through economic integration; critics argue minerals access is the main US aim.

links.actions: France handed over its last base in Chad on 30 January 2025, two months after N'Djamena ended the defence pact.
links.position: Chad says the break is military only, not diplomatic.

links.actions: Cargo flights from Syria to Al-Khadim airbase rose in late 2024; RFI reports the base serves as a hub for Russian arms moving to Mali, Burkina Faso and other Sahel states.
links.returns: A Mediterranean and Sahel logistics hub after Syria.
links.position: Moscow describes its presence as security cooperation at the invitation of Libyan authorities.

links.actions: Sudan's foreign minister said in Feb 2025 the two sides agreed on a 25-year naval logistics point near Port Sudan (up to 4 ships, 300 personnel), pending ratification.
links.position: Khartoum says ratification awaits an elected parliament; the deal is unratified.

links.actions: Niger said in Sept 2025 it wants Rosatom to build two reactors and cooperate on uranium; no construction contract reported.
links.returns: Prospective nuclear and uranium access after Orano's exit.
links.position: Niamey frames it as sovereignty over its uranium.

links.actor: Somali federal government / Puntland vs ISIS-Somalia and al-Shabaab
links.actions: AFRICOM carried out 124 airstrikes in Somalia in 2025, many against ISIS-Somalia in Puntland's Golis Mountains.
links.returns: Counter-terrorism aims; no resource return identified.
links.position: Washington says the strikes protect the US homeland and support Somali forces.

links.actions: US forces left Air Base 201 (Agadez) on 5 Aug 2024 and completed withdrawal from Niger on 15 Sep 2024.
links.returns: n/a (loss of the main US drone base in the Sahel).
links.position: Niamey revoked the military accord, calling it imposed.

links.actions: Niger nationalised SOMAIR in June 2025, removing Orano's 63.4% control; Orano took it to arbitration.
links.returns: Loss of uranium access for Orano (reverse flow).
links.position: Niamey frames it as resource sovereignty; Orano calls it unlawful.

bri.name: Mombasa-Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
bri.lender_builder: China Exim Bank (about 90%); China Road and Bridge Corp built and operated it
bri.china_gets: Building and operating contracts for a Chinese state firm; Libor+3.6% on the commercial loan; a 15-year take-or-pay cargo guarantee
bri.host_position: Kenya's biggest project since independence; Ruto published the loan documents in 2022

bri.name: Addis Ababa-Djibouti Railway
bri.value: About $4bn; Ethiopia's $2.49bn China Exim loan was restructured in 2018 and now matures in 2044
bri.lender_builder: China Exim Bank; CREC and CCECC built it
bri.china_gets: Building contracts for CREC, CCECC and NORINCO; Libor+3% interest; a supply corridor to Djibouti's ports, where China Merchants owns a stake
bri.host_position: Ethiopia's main route to the sea

bri.name: Port de Djibouti / Doraleh stake
bri.value: China Merchants bought 23.5% of Port de Djibouti S.A. for $185m in 2012-13
bri.china_gets: A share in Djibouti's port operator, on the Bab el-Mandeb strait
bri.host_position: Djibouti presents itself as a neutral hub that hosts many countries' bases

bri.name: PLA support base, Djibouti
bri.value: Opened 1 Aug 2017; lease reported at about $20m a year
bri.china_gets: China's first overseas base; about 400 PLA marines and a pier for large warships (US DoD, cited by CRS)
bri.host_position: Beijing calls it a support facility for anti-piracy and evacuation missions

bri.name: Lamu Port (LAPSSET)
bri.lender_builder: Built by China Communications Construction Co; funded by Kenya
bri.china_gets: A building contract for CCCC; no Chinese ownership stake found
bri.host_position: Kenya's gateway to South Sudan and Ethiopia

bri.name: Bagamoyo Port
bri.value: $10bn plan agreed in 2013 with China Merchants and Oman; suspended in 2019; the Chinese partner pulled out in 2022
bri.lender_builder: Formerly China Merchants; now an MoU with AGL (MSC), signed Dec 2025
bri.host_position: Tanzania's ports authority rejected the terms: tax exemptions and the investors' freedom to set port charges

bri.name: Sicomines copper-cobalt (minerals for infrastructure)
bri.value: Up to $7bn of infrastructure under the revised 2024 deal
bri.china_gets: Copper and cobalt output in exchange for infrastructure
bri.host_position: Kinshasa renegotiated the deal for more infrastructure

bri.name: Chinese loans to Africa, 2000-2024
bri.value: $180.87bn in 1,319 loan commitments from 42 lenders (amounts committed, not paid out)
bri.lender_builder: China Exim Bank, China Development Bank and others
bri.china_gets: Interest; contracts for Chinese firms; repayment in resources in some deals
bri.host_position: Governments say they borrowed to fill gaps Western lenders left

bri.name: Top Chinese borrowers in Africa, 2000-2023
bri.value: Angola $46.05bn cumulative; ranking after it: Ethiopia, Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya, Zambia, South Africa, Sudan, Ghana, Cameroon (dollar figures for those not in the brief)
bri.lender_builder: China Exim Bank, China Development Bank
bri.china_gets: Oil-backed repayment in Angola's case; contracts for Chinese firms
bri.host_position: Angola negotiated debt relief in 2024 rather than restructuring

bri.name: Lekki Deep Sea Port
bri.lender_builder: China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) built it; China Development Bank financed
bri.host_position: Lagos calls it Nigeria's first deep-sea port

bri.name: Dar es Salaam port upgrade
bri.value: World Bank-financed berths 1-7, RoRo, channel works
bri.lender_builder: China Harbour Engineering (contractor); World Bank financing
bri.china_gets: Construction contracts only; operators are DP World (berths 4-7) and Adani (CT2)
bri.host_position: Dar es Salaam chose Gulf and Indian operators

bri.name: Kribi deep-water port
bri.value: Container terminal run by KCT consortium
bri.lender_builder: China Harbour Engineering built it; CHEC is a KCT shareholder with CMA CGM and Bollore
bri.china_gets: Shareholding in the terminal operator (exact % not confirmed in a filing)

bri.name: Husab and Rossing uranium
bri.lender_builder: CGN and China-Africa Development Fund (Taurus Minerals, 90% of Swakop Uranium); CNNC's CNUC at Rossing
bri.china_gets: Uranium supply; Namibia's state Epangelo holds 10% of Husab
bri.host_position: Namibia keeps a state stake and royalty

bri.name: Arcadia and Bikita lithium
bri.value: Huayou paid $422m for 100% of Arcadia (completed Apr 2022); Sinomine paid $180m for 74% of Bikita
bri.china_gets: Lithium concentrate for Chinese battery supply chains
bri.host_position: Zimbabwe banned raw lithium ore exports in Dec 2022 to force local processing

who.t: Juntas in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger fight JNIM (al-Qaeda) and Islamic State affiliates; Mali's army works with Russia's Africa Corps, which replaced Wagner in 2025.
Algeria's parliament approved sending troops to Niger in Oct 2026, its first foreign deployment since 1973.

drivers.t: Armed groups tax and protect artisanal gold sites in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, which gives them income and local standing.
The juntas have reasserted state control of mining: Niger moved to nationalise Orano's SOMAIR uranium mine, and Mali began building a Russia-backed refinery.

money.t: SWISSAID found 405 t of African gold entering the UAE in 2022 that African states had not declared as exports; it put 80-85% of African artisanal gold flows through the UAE.
Russia's Yadran Group holds a stake in the planned Mali refinery; Rosatom signed for nuclear reactor plans with Niger.

case.t: Juntas: Western forces failed to stop the insurgency, and control of gold and uranium returns revenue to citizens.
France and Orano: SOMAIR operated under valid agreements, and Orano opposes nationalisation as unlawful.
Russia presents Africa Corps as state-to-state security help requested by Bamako.

avs.t: Russia calls its role partnership with sovereign states; its Africa Corps and allied firms take mining and refinery stakes in Mali.
The UAE says it is tightening due diligence on gold refiners, yet its imports of undeclared African gold remain the largest single flow.

who.t: Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fight the armies of Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad and Niger.
France handed over its last base in Chad in Jan 2025 after Chad ended the defence pact.

drivers.t: Lake Chad shrank by about 90% between 1963 and 2001, cutting fishing, farming and grazing livelihoods.
ISS counted at least 15 ISWAP attacks on remote military outposts in the first half of 2025; defectors said Islamic State sent trainers.

money.t: ISS reports that ISWAP seizes weapons from overrun bases and extorts civilians on the islands it controls.

case.t: Nigeria set up the remote outposts to resettle displaced civilians in destroyed towns.
Chad says ending the French pact restores full sovereignty over its security choices.

who.t: The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have fought since April 2023; the RSF took the SAF headquarters in El Fasher in Oct 2025.
SAF backers: Turkish Baykar drones, Iranian drones and Egyptian support. RSF backers: UAE-linked supply networks found credible by UN experts.

drivers.t: Gold is the main hard-currency source for both sides; the RSF's commercial roots lie in Jebel Amer gold in Darfur.
The war has hit the Gezira farm scheme, Sudan's breadbasket; UN rights chief said drone strikes killed 306 people in three weeks in Oct 2026.

money.t: The UAE imported 29 t of gold directly from Sudan in 2024, plus 18 t from Chad and 9 t from Libya, which SWISSAID calls exit points for RSF gold.
OFAC sanctioned UAE-based firms for supplying the RSF with money and equipment.

case.t: SAF: it is the legitimate national army defending the state against a rebel militia.
RSF: it says it fights a regime of former Bashir-era Islamists.
UAE: it denies arming any party and says its flights carry aid.

avs.t: The UAE publicly backs a ceasefire while UN experts found credible evidence of arms flights to the RSF via eastern Chad.
Iran and Sudan rejected reports of a Red Sea base deal while Iranian drones were reported in SAF use.

who.t: M23/AFC holds much of North and South Kivu; UN experts reported 3,000-4,000 Rwandan troops fighting alongside it.
The US brokered a DRC-Rwanda peace agreement and a regional economic framework in 2025.

drivers.t: Rubaya's coltan mines, held by M23 since April 2024, supply a large share of world tantalum.
Rwanda cites the FDLR, a militia with roots in the 1994 genocide, as a security threat on its border.

money.t: UN experts found at least 150 t of coltan was fraudulently exported from Rubaya to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan output; M23 collected at least $800,000 a month in taxes.
China imported 628,191 t of cobalt intermediates from the DRC in 2024, 98% of its imports by weight.

case.t: Rwanda: it denies backing M23 and says it defends itself against the FDLR.
DRC: it calls M23 a Rwandan proxy looting its minerals.
US: the framework links peace to legal mineral trade and investment.

avs.t: Rwanda denies involvement while UN experts documented its troops and coltan flows into its supply chain.

who.t: President Touadéra won a third term in the Dec 2025 vote, validated with 77.9%; Wagner fighters (about 1,500) and Rwandan troops back his government.

drivers.t: Armed groups and state forces compete over gold, diamond and timber zones; Wagner-linked firms hold gold rights including Ndassima.

money.t: Crisis Group reports that Russians run gold mines, cut timber and receive tax exemptions in return for security; OFAC sanctioned Wagner gold firms.

case.t: Bangui: Russian and Rwandan forces delivered security gains that UN peacekeeping did not.
Moscow presses for Africa Corps, under its defence ministry, to replace Wagner and for CAR to pay more.

avs.t: Russia describes its role as security cooperation, while Wagner-controlled firms earn from gold and timber concessions.

who.t: Ethiopia and Eritrea traded threats over Ethiopian claims to Eritrea's Assab port through 2025; Eritrea signed a security pact with Egypt.
In Somalia, AFRICOM ran 124 strikes in 2025 against ISIS-Somalia and al-Shabaab.

drivers.t: Ethiopia opened the GERD dam in Sept 2025; Egypt says it threatens its Nile water.
Landlocked Ethiopia's leaders call sea access existential.

money.t: China financed and built the Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway and runs its first overseas military base in Djibouti.

case.t: Ethiopia: GERD is a development project and sea access a peaceful goal.
Eritrea: Ethiopia's push is irredentism and a red line.
Egypt: the dam was filled without a binding agreement.

avs.t: Abiy ruled out war over sea access in Mar 2025; later his army chief and an ambassador spoke of taking Assab back.

who.t: JNIM has spread from the Sahel into northern Benin and Togo; Benin said 54 soldiers died in an April 2025 attack.

drivers.t: Artisanal gold reached 39% of Ghana's output in 2024.
Lekki port in Nigeria (CHEC 52.5%) and Côte d'Ivoire's Baleine field anchor coastal investment.

money.t: The UAE imported 52 t of gold from Togo in 2024, a country that produces almost none.

case.t: Benin's government at first said eight soldiers died, then acknowledged 54.

avs.t: Benin's initial toll of eight was revised to 54 after JNIM claimed 70.

who.t: An Islamic State-linked insurgency in Cabo Delgado is fought by Mozambique's army and over 4,000 Rwandan troops.

drivers.t: TotalEnergies' $20bn Mozambique LNG project lifted force majeure in Oct 2025.
Zimbabwe's artisanal miners produce most of its gold, bought by the state's Fidelity refinery.

money.t: The EU funded the Rwandan deployment through the European Peace Facility.
Chinese firms bought Zimbabwe's Arcadia and Bikita lithium mines.

case.t: Mozambique says the Rwandan troops are rotations under a bilateral agreement, not an escalation.
ACLED notes Rwanda's counter-insurgency record but limits to civilian protection.

avs.t: Kigali presents its Mozambique mission as security help; the deployment protects the LNG zone it helps reopen.

who.t: Libya is split between Tripoli and Haftar's eastern LNA, which hosts Russian Africa Corps logistics at al-Khadim airbase.

drivers.t: Oil revenue is split between rival authorities; the east shut fields in Aug 2024.
Algeria supplies gas to Europe via Medgaz and approved sending troops to Niger in Oct 2026.

money.t: The UAE imported 27 t of gold from Egypt and 9 t from Libya in 2024.

avs.t: Russia frames Africa Corps as state-to-state partnership; flight tracking showed a spike in Russian military flights from Syria to eastern Libya, and al-Khadim became a hub for arms bound for the Sahel.
